narrative:
Based on the assessment, there is a 23% chance you will fail your final year. While this may not seem high, our school's policy requires additional support for any student whose risk exceeds 10%, which is why you are being asked to complete remedial courses. Think of this as an early safety net, not a punishment.

Three factors most strongly shaped this assessment, though interestingly, all three actually worked in your favor rather than against you.

The most influential factor was your clean academic record — you have no history of failed classes whatsoever, which strongly suggests you have the capability to succeed. This was the single biggest reason your risk score wasn't even higher.

The second most important factor was your ambition. You have expressed a clear desire to pursue higher education, and every student who is not currently flagged for remedial courses shares this same goal. Your motivation is a genuine asset.

Third, your weekend social habits were considered. Your alcohol consumption on weekends is low, which again pushed your risk downward. Students not required to take remedial courses show a range of habits here, so your moderation is a positive sign.

So why are you still being asked to take remedial courses? Your overall profile, when all factors are considered together, still places you above the school's cautious 10% threshold. Some background factors in your home environment appear to contribute to this.

The remedial courses are designed to strengthen your foundation before it becomes a problem. Attend them consistently, and your strong track record suggests you are well-positioned to pass.
